'''James Khristian "Khris" Middleton''' (born August 12, 1991 in [[Charleston, South Carolina]]) is an [[United States|American]] [[college basketball]] player with the [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team]] who is entering his [[2011–12 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|junior season]]. He attended [[Porter-Gaud School]], where he was coached by John Pearson. As a junior and senior, he was named South Carolina Player of the year, and was a [[McDonald's All-American]] nominee. Middleton chose to matriculate at [[Texas A&M University]], where he started the majority of the games in his freshman year. In his sophomore season, he was named to the All-Big 12 Second Team after leading the Aggies in scoring at a 14.4 point per game clip.

==Early life and high school career==
[[File:Josh Powell cropped.jpg|thumb|left|Josh Powell is a professional basketball player and the cousin of Middleton.]]
Middleton was born on August 12, 1991 in [[Charleston, South Carolina]] to James and Nichelle Middleton. His cousin, [[Josh Powell]], has played in the NBA. Another cousin, Kenny Manigault, plays basketball at [[Wichita State University]] and was teammates with Khris on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) team Carolina Celtics.<ref>{{cite news|first=Philip|last=Bowman|url=http://www.postandcourier.com/news/2008/aug/06/pinewood_star_manigault_commits_wichita_49879/|title=Pinewood star Manigault commits to Wichita State|work=[[The Post and Courier]]|publisher=[[Evening Post Publishing Company]]|date=August 6, 2008|accessdate=August 30, 2011}}</ref> Two other teammates on the Carolina Celtics accepted Division I basketball scholarships, Jamal Curry ([[Radford Highlanders men's basketball|Radford]]) and Devin Booker ([[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]]).<ref name=TexasA&Mbio>{{cite web|url=http://www.aggieathletics.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=27300&ATCLID=205236051|title=#22 Khris Middleton|work=[[Texas A&M Aggies]]|publisher=[[Texas A&M University]]|accessdate=August 18, 2011}}</ref>

Middleton attended [[Porter-Gaud School]] and played basketball for the Cyclones under coach John Pearson. As a sophomore, he averaged 12 points and eight rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite news|first=Philip|last=Bowman|url=http://www.postandcourier.com/news/2007/dec/06/overnight_sensation24183/|title=Successful spring rockets Khris Middleton up recruiting rankings|work=[[The Post and Courier]]|publisher=[[Evening Post Publishing Company]]|date=December 6, 2007|accessdate=August 28, 2011}}</ref> In his junior season, Middleton posted averages of 21 points and 8.6 rebounds per game and was named state player of the year. He repeated as player of the year as a senior, scoring 22.4 points per game and grabbing 8.6 rebounds per game in leading Porter-Gaud to the state title game.<ref name=TexasA&Mbio/> Middleton was named Most Valuable Player of the Porter-Gaud Holiday Classic, scoring 22 points in the championship.<ref>{{cite news|first=Philip|last=Bowman|url=http://news.google.com/newspapers?id=PZVIAAAAIBAJ&sjid=0AkNAAAAIBAJ&pg=6266,2499232&dq=khris-middleton+porter-gaud&hl=en|title=Middleton Powers Cyclones To Victory‎|work=[[The Post and Courier]]|publisher=[[Evening Post Publishing Company]]|date=December 23, 2008|accessdate=August 31, 2011}}</ref> He was nominated for the [[2009 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], but was not selected to participate.<ref>{{cite news|first=Philip|last=Bowman|url=http://www.postandcourier.com/news/2009/feb/19/jennings_picked_mcdonalds_all_american_g72287/|title=Jennings picked for McDonald's All-American game|work=[[The Post and Courier]]|publisher=[[Evening Post Publishing Company]]|date=February 19, 2009|accessdate=August 31, 2011}}</ref>

ESPN ranked him the 64th best prospect in the Class of 2009, and noted he was the best shooter at his position. Middleton was recruited by [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]], [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]], [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]], [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], and [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's]].<ref name=TexasA&Mbio/> He chose Texas A&M, and signed with the Aggies on May 30, 2008. He liked the college town atmosphere, and got along well with the coaching staff.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.postandcourier.com/news/2008/may/30/porter_gauds_middleton_commits_texas_a_a42759/|title=Porter-Gaud's Middleton commits to Texas A&M|work=[[The Post and Courier]]|publisher=[[Evening Post Publishing Company]]|date=May 30, 2008|accessdate=August 31, 2011}}</ref>

==College career==
===Freshman===
Coming into his freshman year, Middleton expected to fill the [[three-point shot|three point shooting]] void of departed senior [[Josh Carter]]. Middleton's college career started slowly, connecting on 1-of-12 [[field goal (basketball)|field goal]]s in limited action of his first three games.<ref>{{cite news|first=Brent|last=Zwerneman|url=http://www.chron.com/sports/college/article/Freshman-Middleton-in-middle-of-action-for-A-M-men-1708248.php|title=Freshman Middleton in middle of action for A&M men|work=[[Houston Chronicle]]|publisher=[[Hearst Corporation]]|date=February 13, 2010|accessdate=August 31, 2011}}</ref> After a season-ending leg injury to Derrick Roland on December 11, 2009, Middleton was forced to take a larger role in the offense and started 18 of the last 20 games. On February 3, 2010, he scored 16 points to help Texas A&M erase an 11-point second half deficit to defeat [[2009–10 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]] 77-74.<ref>{{cite news|first=Steve|last=Walentik|url=http://www.columbiatribune.com/news/2011/jan/15/well-worth-the-wait/|title=A&M's Middleton no longer a surprise|work=[[Columbia Daily Tribune]]|date=January 15, 2011|accessdate=September 1, 2011}}</ref> In a 69-53 [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]] Round of 64 victory over [[2009–10 Utah State Aggies men's basketball team|Utah State]], Middleton scored a season-high 19 points on 7-of-10 shooting.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300780245|title=Middleton helps Texas A&M snag fifth straight opening round win|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=March 19, 2010|accessdate=September 2, 2011}}</ref> Texas A&M's season ended with a loss in the Round of 32 to [[2009–10 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]]; the Aggies finished with a record of 24-10.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300802509|title=Kramer takes over to lead Purdue to sixth Sweet 16 in 12 appearances|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=March 21, 2010|accessdate=September 2, 2011}}</ref> Overall Khris Middleton averaged 7.2 points and 3.7 rebounds per game and led the team in scoring five times.<ref name=TexasA&Mbio/>

===Sophomore===
As a sophomore, Middleton led the team and finished ninth in the Big 12 in scoring at 14.4 points per game while also contributing 5.2 rebounds per game. He hit 45.2 percent of his shots from the floor and 78.4 percent of his [[free throws]]. Middleton scored in excess of 10 points in 27 games and led the team in scoring 16 times.<ref name=TexasA&Mbio/> He scored a career-high 31 points in a 71-62 overtime victory over [[2010–11 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]], including 11 of the team's las 12 points in regulation. This earned him Big 12 Player of the Week and Oscar Robertson National Player of the Week honors for the week of December 13–19, 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2011/oscar101221.html|work=[[United States Basketball Writers Association|U.S. Basketball Writers Association]]|title=Texas A&M's Middleton is Oscar Robertson National Player of the Week|accessdate=September 20, 2011|date=December 21, 2010}}</ref> On January 15, 2011, Middleton tallied 28 points, including 11 in overtime, to defeat [[2010–11 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]] 91-89.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310150245|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|title=Khris Middleton tallies 11 points in OT as Aggies take out Tigers|accessdate=October 29, 2011|date=January 15, 2011}}</ref>

===Junior===
Prior to Middleton's junior season, head coach [[Mark Turgeon]] left to take the same position at the [[University of Maryland]] and was replaced by [[Billy Kennedy (basketball)|Billy Kennedy]] of [[Murray State Racers men's basketball|Murray State]]. Middleton was impressed with Kennedy's coaching acumen and chose to remain an Aggie.<ref>{{cite news|first=Jimmy|last=Burch|url=http://www.star-telegram.com/2011/07/07/3207616/new-texas-ams-new-basketball-coach.html|title=New Texas A&M's new basketball coach will install faster pace|work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|publisher=[[The McClatchy Company]]|date=July 7, 2011|accessdate=August 28, 2011}}</ref> He was listed on the preseason watchlist for the [[Wooden Award]].<ref name=wooden>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/7053604/opposing-coaches-break-50-players-wooden-award-watch-list-college-basketball|title=Scouting the Wooden Award watch list|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=October 3, 2011|accessdate=October 29, 2011}}</ref> Middleton was a unanimous choice to the preseason All-Big 12 team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=106110&SPID=13134&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=10410&ATCLID=205312119|title=Preseason All-Big 12 Men's Basketball Honors Announced|work=[[Big 12 Conference]]|date=October 6, 2011|accessdate=October 29, 2011}}</ref>
